content: For what else is tragedy, but the sufferings of men, bewildered by their admiration of external things, represented in proper verse?
author: Epictetus
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Human beings are never a finished product; we exist in perpetual transit between our basic instincts and our highest potential. The tension we feel inside is not a flaw—it is the very engine of self-evolution.

In Epictetus's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Growing into a fuller version of yourself requires crossing uncertain territory with no safety net. You have to be willing to outgrow the comfort of familiar limitations to step into who you are capable of becoming.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
